correctness.rationale: The arclength centroid is exactly (0, hs/[2(1+s)]). Strict convexity and reflection reduce global Euclidean median coincidence to the zero of the verified closed-form vertical derivative G(h). Both endpoint signs are strict, and a 50-decimal-place outward-rounded interval certificate on 100 rational subintervals establishes G′(h)>0.09 throughout [0.7,0.8]. Thus the root exists uniquely in the interval and the median order reverses; independent high-precision edge quadrature checks the normalization and integral formula. No global uniqueness outside the interval is claimed.

value.rationale: The geometric median and Spieker centroid are two intrinsic and naturally motivated ways to center a uniform triangular wireframe; equality is not forced by convexity except in highly symmetric cases. The isolated non-equilateral coincidence disproves a plausible equilateral-only rigidity inference and determines the exact side of the change in their vertical ordering, with a complete rigorous local shape characterization. This is an exact triangle-center phenomenon, not a generic numerical approximation or arbitrary parameter slice.
